en.title: Minimum Flips to Get an Alternating Binary String
en.description:
Each operation flips one bit; make all adjacent characters different and find the minimum number of flips. The empty string already satisfies the condition. The source statement body is missing; the operation was recovered from the title and the original example's bit-by-bit flip explanation. In the original example, flipping the 1st and 3rd bits (1-indexed) of 111101 gives 010101, so the answer is 2; the 101010 written in the original example is a typo for the target string.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric constraints are explicitly marked as this site's additions.
en.input: The first line contains the length n, and the second line contains the binary string (an empty line when n=0). Full original bounds: 0≤n≤200000, and the string contains only 0 and 1.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 1; 2; 0. These answers were verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Once the first bit of an alternating string is fixed, the remaining bits are determined. Count the number of mismatches d against 0101…; the mismatch count for the other target is n−d.
